content.overview: Water pollution control in India is governed primarily by the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974, which establishes Pollution Control Boards and regulates discharge of sewage and trade effluents through a consent regime. The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 provides umbrella standards and powers. NGT may hear Schedule I environmental civil questions. Constitutional Articles 21, 48A and 51A(g) supply supporting duties and rights doctrine.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Discharge into water? (2) Consent under Water Act? (3) EPA standards exceeded? (4) NGT or Board enforcement?
content.study:
Identify the water medium first. Water Act consent for sewage and trade effluent is the operational core; EPA standards and NGT relief may apply concurrently.

No new case invented. Vellore context retained in doctrine topics where issue matches.

sections.heading: Water Act 1974
sections.body: Prevents and controls water pollution; Central and State Boards; regulation of sewage and trade effluent discharge; consent requirements as enacted.

sections.heading: Consent regime
sections.body: Discharge without required consent or in breach of conditions attracts statutory consequences under the Water Act.

sections.heading: EPA interface
sections.body: EPA discharge standards and Central directions may apply alongside Water Act duties.

sections.heading: Enforcement and forum
sections.body: Board directions and prosecution support; NGT for Schedule I civil environmental claims; High Court under Art. 226 where maintainable.

sections.heading: Constitutional layer
sections.body: Art. 21 healthy-environment doctrine; Arts. 48A and 51A(g) duties.

examples.title: Trade effluent without consent
examples.body: Factory discharges trade effluent into a stream without State Board consent — Water Act consent and enforcement framework applies.

hypotheticals.question: Does NGT jurisdiction remove the need for Water Act consent?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Consent remains a statutory compliance duty; NGT provides a civil remedial forum for environmental questions within its jurisdiction.

misconceptions.trap: Only EPA applies to water pollution; Water Act is obsolete.
misconceptions.correction: Water Act remains the primary medium-specific consent statute; EPA is the umbrella statute.
